metadata.description: Log Analytics workspace name that Microsoft Sentinel is enabled on
Resource name of the analytics rule 'MDE - Ransomware-Style Mass File Rename Per Device'

properties.displayName: MDE - Ransomware-Style Mass File Rename Per Device
properties.description:
Detects a device renaming an unusually large number of files to a different
extension inside a short window — the encryption pass of a ransomware
payload. Aggregating rename volume per device (rather than alerting per file)
keeps the alert count at one per infected host and survives the low-and-slow
variants that throttle encryption to stay under per-process thresholds.
properties.query:
let rename_threshold = 300;
let bucket = 15m;
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where ActionType == "FileRenamed"
| extend OldExt = tolower(tostring(extract(@"\.([A-Za-z0-9]{1,10})$", 1, PreviousFileName)))
| extend NewExt = tolower(tostring(extract(@"\.([A-Za-z0-9]{1,10})$", 1, FileName)))
// An encryption pass changes the extension. A move or a folder rename keeps
// it, so requiring a *change* removes most of the routine rename noise.
| where isnotempty(NewExt) and NewExt != OldExt
| summarize RenamedFiles = dcount(FileName),
            NewExtensions = make_set(NewExt, 10),
            ExampleFiles = make_set(FileName, 10),
            Folder = any(FolderPath),
            FirstRename = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastRename = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, bucket)
| where RenamedFiles >= rename_threshold
| extend RenamesPerSecond = round(RenamedFiles / (bucket / 1s), 2)
// Sentinel cannot entity-map an array (make_set) column, so project a single
// representative file path as a scalar for the File entity.
| extend ExampleFile = tostring(ExampleFiles[0])
| project TimeGenerated = FirstRename, LastRename, DeviceId, DeviceName,
          AccountName, RenamedFiles, RenamesPerSecond, NewExtensions,
          ExampleFile, Folder

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{RenamedFiles}} files were renamed to a different extension on {{DeviceName}} under account {{AccountName}} within 15 minutes — consistent with a ransomware encryption pass.
